statute_opened.amendment: Elections Law section 57(ט)(1) is changed from the 47th day to the 49th day before election day. Section 57(ט)(3) changes from the 52nd day to the 55th day. The PDF text does not print a clock time or a September date.

events.derived_if_election_day_is_2026_10_27: The 49th day before 27 October 2026 is 8 September 2026. That derivation is not a date printed in the statute. The old calendar date 2026-09-09 does not match a 49-day count.

where_seen: Existing calendar isr_2026.json, as_of 2026-08-08, citing Wikipedia and the committee home URL.
The Petek schema.org text, opened, says the election is 27 October 2026. That site is an aggregator.
N12 articles in this window speak of the election being two weeks away, which matches this date, but the opened poll article does not print 27 October.

news_source.what_it_says: CEC chair Noam Sohlberg ruled that day that, if the 25th Knesset serves out its term, the next election is 27 October 2026, 16 Heshvan 5787, four years and ten days after the 1 November 2022 election. He cited Basic Law: The Knesset section 8 as the reason not to stretch the term to about five years.

events.known_from_opened_text: i24 and Israel National News say the committee will submit the results to the president on Wednesday 4 November 2026, subject to minor corrections from the routine integrity review. The results page at votes26.bechirot.gov.il returned HTTP 202 and no table. The old wiki note is no longer the only place this date appears, and the submission has not been opened.

The Ynet explainer of 11 October 2026 says agreements may be signed until 11 days before election day, subject to Central Elections Committee approval, and that this cycle's date is 16 October because the election is 27 October. That sentence is in the opened article. It is not the statute.
events.news_after_the_date: Ynet on 16 October 2026, 12:12 Israel time, says the signing process at the Central Elections Committee offices ended Friday at noon, and that Amcha and the reservists' list did not sign with each other. Kikar the same day lists five previously announced pairs and says the notification day was still open. Neither page is the filed register.

events.known_from_opened_text: The 19 October Ynet article on Gantz says soldier voting opens the next day. The committee page was not opened.
Kikar on 16 October says voting at Israeli missions abroad started the day before. This is not the 20 October date in the August wiki calendar, and it is not an official page.

events.label_ko: 이중봉투까지 센 뒤 위원회가 발표했다고 보도된 의석
events.known_from_opened_text: i24 says the committee published the allocation on the night between Thursday and Friday. Israel National News timestamps its story 30 Oct 2026, 00:50 GMT+2. Both print Likud 27, Yashar 21, Together 12, Joint List 11, Democrats 8, Ra'am 8, Yisrael Beiteinu 7, Otzma 7, United Torah Judaism 7, Shas 6, Religious Zionism 6. Turnout 77.9%. Counted 5,716,665, valid 5,690,778, invalid 25,887. Threshold 184,947 votes. The same articles say this is still subject to minor corrections.

Acting CEC director Dean Livne says the Shin Bet head brought classified information to chairman Noam Sohlberg the day before, an inquiry was opened, and the main points were also given to Netanyahu, Yair Lapid and Gadi Eisenkot. Livne says the inquiry does not affect the results that will be submitted to the president and is not about a particular sector. No finding is printed.

Herzog said Thursday night that factions totaling 67 recommended Eisenkot and factions totaling 46 recommended Netanyahu. i24 says United Torah Judaism named nobody. He said he would assign the mandate the coming Sunday. That Sunday was 8 November. A 7 November note in this pack dated it 9 November. The president's own site was not opened.

N12, published 8 November 2026 at 16:45 and updated 17:23, says Herzog assigned the task to Gadi Eisenkot under Basic Law: The Government section 7 after saying the official results had been received. The president's house restated 67, 46 and one faction of seven. N12 reports 28 days, with a presidential addition of up to 14 days. The statute page and the CEC results page were not opened. No government was formed.

The Times of Israel on 10 November says the 26th Knesset was set to be sworn in that day. Articles opened on 15 and 16 November treat the Knesset as already in session and discuss a speaker vote still ahead. The official swearing notice was not opened.

events.label_ko: 의장 투표가 다음 날 본회의로 예고됨
events.known_from_opened_text: Israel Hayom on 16 November 2026, updated 15:13, says the speaker vote is the next day's plenum and United Torah Judaism had not decided. Makor Rishon the same day says Kahana refused Smotrich's two conditions. No result is printed. A 16:00 clock appears only in pages that were not opened, so it is not recorded.

i24, Kan and Globes say Kahana was elected on 17 November with 66 votes in favor. Kan and Globes say Ofir Katz received 52 on his own ballot. Ynet's short item was written while Katz's ballot was still ahead. i24 says 61 signatures were filed. The Knesset roll was not opened.

events.label_ko: 야샤르·리쿠드 두 번째 협상, 합의 없음
events.known_from_opened_text: Makor Rishon says the Herzliya meeting lasted more than four hours. The joint statement says positions were presented and a follow-up will be held. No government.

Israel Hayom, updated 08:52, and Channel 14 that morning say the teams meet at the Knesset on 23 November. The Jerusalem Post, updated 12:46, prints the time as 18:00. None of those pages contains a result.

Channel 14 on 23 November says the mandate given to Eisenkot is expected to expire on 6 December. The statute page was not opened. N12 on 8 November reported 28 days plus up to 14 without printing this date.
